name: Mi
description: 30-line zero-config CLI agent for bug fixes and refactoring. An autonomous coding agent that fits in a single JavaScript file with no framework or dependencies beyond Node builtins. Works with any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenAI, Ollama, local models). Includes bash tool for full system access and skills tool for markdown playbooks loaded on demand. Optimized for running with local LLMs with minimal token usage.
community_quotes: how small can an agentic harness be and remain useful? turns out, very small. Claude Code is ~500k lines of code, OpenCode is ~100k, mi is 30 lines, yet, it has all the features expected from agentic harness
mi is optimised for running with local LLMs, it's concise and to the point. it can extend itself to solve task with fewer tokens
mi is a loop, two tools, and an LLM that you plug in

name: Linchpin
description: Open-source, self-hostable runtime for managed AI agents under Apache-2.0 license. Deploy with single 'docker compose up' command to get a full agent platform with REST + SSE API, per-session Docker sandbox, MCP tools, encrypted vaults. Bring any cloud model via OpenRouter or local via Ollama. Includes versioned agent configs, environment templates, 8 built-in tools (bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, web_fetch, web_search), Fernet-encrypted credential vaults, and event log persistence.
community_quotes: Every time Devin, Manus, or Operator launched, the top comment on HN was some variant of 'is this open source?' The answer kept being no. So we built Linchpin.
Closer to 'LangGraph + your-own-FastAPI + your-own-docker-py + your-own-event-log, but pre-wired' than to a library

name: BossHogg
description: Agent-first CLI for PostHog analytics and feature flags. Gives AI coding agents and terminal-native developers a compact, scriptable way to operate PostHog without loading a large MCP tool surface into every session. Supports HogQL queries, feature flags, persons, groups, cohorts, events, insights, dashboards, experiments, and production-safe analytics operations with --json output, stable error codes, auth redaction, and HTTPS-only releases.
community_quotes: MCPs have a purpose. CLIs have a purpose. PostHog MCP is great for rich assistant workflows, web UI parity, and chart-oriented exploration. But when you are working inside Claude Code, Cursor, scripts, or CI, you often want something smaller and more deterministic: a CLI your agent can call on demand.
Designed to be practical and safe: --json everywhere, stable error codes, auth redaction, HTTPS-only release builds, HogQL auto-LIMIT, --yes gating for destructive operations

name: xyOps
description: Open-source operations automation platform for self-hosted teams under BSD-3-Clause license. Schedule jobs, build visual workflows, monitor servers, trigger alerts, capture snapshots, and coordinate incident response from one app. Run plugins written in any language via JSON over STDIO, collect server metrics with xySat, store secrets, buckets, roles, API keys, and web hooks. Full app feature set is open source including SSO - no enterprise fork, no license key, no telemetry. Paid plans are support subscriptions only.
community_quotes: I built xyOps because I kept seeing technical teams stitch together the same pile of tools: cron jobs, shell scripts, workflow builders, monitoring dashboards, web hooks, and incident notes.

The full app is open source under BSD-3-Clause. There is no separate enterprise fork, no hidden feature set, no license key, and no telemetry pushed back to us. Paid plans are support subscriptions only.

name: Mycelis
description: Serverless AI workspace with smart routing and MCP agents. Abstracts hardware completely - instantly spin up open-source models on optimized GPUs or bring your own keys (BYOK). Acts as unified OpenAI-compatible API gateway for coding clients like OpenCode, desktop apps, or scripts. Features conditional smart routing to optimal models, vector-powered semantic cache to slash costs, integrated RAG, native MCP agents for GitHub/Slack/Discord, and per-minute usage billing with zero server maintenance.
community_quotes: I spent a lot of time thinking about the mounting expenses with AI over the last months and came to the conclusion that routing specific tasks to the most optimal model is the absolute best way forward.
You shouldn't have to keep an expensive cloud GPU idling 24/7 or write endless custom wrappers just to connect an LLM to your database or tools.
The tech stack relies on a .NET 10 backend, PostgreSQL, Qdrant for semantic caching, and a Node.js gateway for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool integrations.
